summary: Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Bokar Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche, whom he also taught.

Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (1879–1941) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (~1898–1912), Kunzang Pelden (~1900–1926), and Shenphen Nangwa.
Khenpo Nüden studied under Shechen Gyaltsab (~1910–1925) and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (~1920–1941), and taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin, Lama Zolpa Trinlé, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1960–1981), later serving as principal teacher at Rumtek Monastery's shedra (~1977).

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying under teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche (~1959–1987), he taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970) and at the University of Virginia (~1979–1980).

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under teachers including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenpo Nüden, later holding posts at Men-Tsee-Khang and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1959–1968).
Khyenrab Norbu (1882–1962) was a Tibetology scholar. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, including professor emeritus attested in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of Otago (attested 2015) under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie. In 2013, he also studied under Jinhua Chen and other scholars.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the First Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Freiburg. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1923–1945), dean at Hokkaido University, and professor at Chuo University.
Kien T. Le is a Buddhist studies student who pursued an MDiv at Harvard University (2023–2026) before becoming a PhD student at Indiana University Bloomington in 2026.
Kim Gutschow works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University and has held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott (born 1955) is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She held academic posts at the University of Leeds (~1980–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012–2021).
Kim Lam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who has held posts at Deakin University's Melbourne Burwood Campus and as a Research Officer at Western Sydney University.

Kim Plofker (born 1964) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. After earning her PhD under David Pingree at Brown University, she taught at MIT and held visiting positions before joining Union College, becoming Associate Professor in 2019.

Kimberley C. Patton (born 1958) is a religious studies scholar who completed her doctorate at Harvard University (~1984–1992). She served as Assistant Professor (~1990–2001) and Professor of the Comparative and Historical Study of Religion (~2001) at Harvard.

Kimiaki Tanaka (born 1955) works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts as assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1989), visiting professor at Beijing Center for Japanese Studies (2003), and researcher at the Eastern Institute.
